parsed.explanation: Combined regime stacks universal border exposure (sex-doubt visa refusals, X markers ended, reported passport confiscation/stranding, fraud-referral risk) with state facility exclusion on state-owned buildings, a documented arrest-to-birth-sex-custody pathway, and national custody abuse (forced labor, beatings, sexual abuse; conversion-therapy prison policies). Adult public-facility care bans bite, though emergency care and private-pay options remain. Offsetting: no identity criminalisation, private sphere largely open, functioning courts with active litigation, legal-aid guidance, national hate-crime and employment protections. Severity of custody and document exposures exceeds 0.35 exclusion-only anchors; remedy function and absence of routine street targeting keep it above 0.25.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable: document discrepancy or doubt about sex → refuse case, request evidence; suspected misrepresentation → consider lifetime fraud ineligibility. X markers ended; travelers report passports confiscated/blocked, stranded abroad; eight-plus foreign governments issued advisories. Nov 2025 Supreme Court let restrictions take effect.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four elements, never automatic, limited waivers exist; civil-liberties suit pending; legal-aid FAQ tracks document rules. Existing X passports valid until expiration.
entry_documents.interaction: Document/presentation mismatch also triggers airport secondary screening and pat-down outing; a refusal can cascade into custody where documented abuse applies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men report forced labor, beatings, solitary for refusal, severe sexual abuse. From 2026 corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal). Trans woman arrested in restroom held 24 hours in men's ward — documented birth-sex placement chain.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; functioning courts; legal-aid and ACLU litigation; consular/attorney access not documented as barred.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility-rule arrest → birth-sex custody → hostile custody environment; document fraud allegation → immigration detention → documented abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State 2023 executive order applies birth-sex definitions to all state-owned facilities (bathrooms, changing rooms, shelters, incarceration); K-12 bans 2022 and 2025. National executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities. Region shows arrest precedent under analogous laws (trespass, up to 60 days).
federal_state_facilities.protection: Trespass in the cited model requires willful entry plus refusal to depart when asked; private settings largely unaffected; no documented prosecution under this state's own rule.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Government buildings a visitor may enter (capitol, agencies, possibly publicly run transport) become criminal-exposure sites; arrest feeds custody chain above.

care_services.exposure: SB 904 (signed 14 May 2026, effective immediately) bars public funds, Medicaid, and state facilities/properties for gender-affirming care to adults and minors; employee violations a misdemeanor. National orders restrict federal funding.
care_services.protection: Emergency treatment to prevent death or major impairment exempted; mental-health counseling, intersex care, complication treatment exempted; privately owned facilities with private insurance/out-of-pocket remain available.
care_services.interaction: Visitor with no Medicaid relies on private pay; emergency presentation is protected but routine HRT continuity at public facilities is not.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy targets groups 'radically pro-transgender'; DOJ rhetoric and 'gender ideology' enforcement directives; state has no gender-identity discrimination or hate-crime coverage, no-promo-homo law, diversity-training ban; 2025 poll: 66% support sex-on-documents laws.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute and Bostock employment ruling remain in force; counterterrorism memo states it will not target mere disagreement; reward criteria do not list gender ideology.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises social-hostility and police-discretion risk at encounters that begin as document or facility checks.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for minors in public settings; K-12 facility bans by birth sex; national executive order directs criminal investigation of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; 2024 Nex Benedict death after school bathroom beating (resident case).
minors_guardians.protection: Emergency and private-pay care exempted; visiting minors not enrolled avoid school rules; parental consent issues not documented as traveler-facing.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling trans minor needing non-emergency care at a public facility faces refusal; an incident at a visited school triggers facility rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Resident-directed hostility documented (2018 death threats to a 12-year-old; school bathroom violence); no state hate-crime coverage; conservative climate signals. No violence incident against a trans visitor is documented either way.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute prosecutable in national court; general US homicide background applies; no organized targeting or moral-police sweeps documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street encounters are most likely to escalate when tied to document or facility checks rather than free-standing violence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit unresolved after Supreme Court allowed the restriction; HB 1225 final status unresolved; driver's-licence marker status unsourced; July 2026 risk-map grade for this state unstated; state-level recourse thin (no GI statutes).
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts with multiple injunctions against executive orders; active civil-liberties litigation; legal-aid FAQ; national protections enforceable; remedies documented working in some challenges.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Contested national posture means exposure varies by date of travel; partial injunctions mitigate but do not remove the document and facility regimes.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra offers universal discretionary exclusion with no remedy and no custody harm. This jurisdiction's document regime is similarly exclusionary but with fraud-referral severity, and it adds criminal facility exposure plus documented custodial abuse — worse in severity — while functioning courts, pending litigation and waiver mechanisms give better recourse than Vellandra's rubber-stamp appeal.

Vesskar's routine biometric checkpoint exposure, verification detention, care denial and slow remedies closely match this dossier's border and care profile. This case rates slightly lower because documented state custody abuse and an arrest-to-men's-ward pathway add severity beyond Vesskar's administrative holds, though its private sphere is more open than Vesskar's linked-card everyday exposure.

Kestrel Isles' secondary screening, discretionary entry refusal and administrative outcomes with slow appeals understate this dossier: refusals here can carry fraud/eligibility consequences, facilities are criminalised in government buildings, and detention carries documented abuse. This jurisdiction is materially less safe than the 0.55 anchor despite similar entry mechanics.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: a federal document/entry regime that disbelieves sex-ambiguous papers (refusal, stranding, fraud referral) feeding into a state facility regime that criminalises restroom use on state property, whose arrest pathway already produced birth-sex ward placement elsewhere in the region, and into national custody environments with documented abuse. Care is restricted in public settings but emergency and private-pay routes survive. Everyday private life remains largely open, courts function and litigate, and no visitor-specific violence is recorded — but the documented exposures are universal or state-imposed, and the key remedies (passport challenge, marker litigation) remain unresolved, so recourse has not yet changed outcomes.
